correctness.rationale: Fixing selected original vertices A, every subdivided edge internal to G[A] is forced selected; selected subdivision edges internal to B=V\A must form a matching, and each B-vertex not covered by that matching independently chooses none or one selected cross edge into A. These necessary and sufficient conditions prove the generating polynomial bijectively for arbitrary finite simple G, including disconnected graphs. In K_n, choose |A|=a and j-matching in K_{n-a}; the support for a>=1 is the full interval [a(a+1)/2, n+a(a-1)/2], and summing gaps max(0,2a-n) gives floor((n-1)^2/4); a=0 gives no additional positive sizes. For any connected G, a proper convex set must omit at least one original vertex; its internal edges exclude >=delta(G) originals, and each omitted vertex supports at most one extra selected subdivision edge, giving |C|<=|V|+|E|-delta(G), attained by omitting one min-degree vertex and selecting exactly one cross subdivision. Independent brute all 8 graphs on 3 vertices, all 64 on 4 vertices, and seven five-vertex graphs reproduced the matching-expansion coefficients.
